purpose: Separate scheduler/worker queue behavior from GitHub repository behavior without creating excessive automated traffic.

system_boundary.scheduler_worker_layer: creates or delays the GitHub write request
system_boundary.github_layer: receives the write, creates repository commit, exposes commit timestamp and DAG
system_boundary.key_warning: A delayed or stale automation execution is not by itself a GitHub vulnerability.

live_test_rules: Do not perform volumetric or excessive automated traffic against GitHub.
Do not run rapid-fire 50-write bursts or per-second overwrite storms against production GitHub infrastructure.
Use only repositories and accounts owned by the researcher.
Prefer additive unique files over destructive overwrites.
Use independent nonce and SHA-256 per lane.
Record task-registration acknowledgement time, scheduled target, scheduler run visibility, Git commit time, and Git DAG parent order separately.
Stop if rate-limit, abuse, service-degradation, or unexpected third-party impact signals appear.
For any higher-volume test, obtain explicit authorization from GitHub Bug Bounty first.

safe_next_gate.name: LOW_VOLUME_VALID_VS_INVALID_QUEUE_ISOLATION
safe_next_gate.design: small controlled batches only, with generous spacing and no attempt to stress capacity
safe_next_gate.primary_question: Does stale or delayed execution reproduce independently of invalid symbolic time strings?
safe_next_gate.github_specific_escalation_condition: Only escalate as a GitHub vulnerability if contradictory or unsafe GitHub-side behavior is demonstrated independently of the external scheduler, such as impossible repository DAG/state behavior, authorization failure, or a GitHub-owned queue flaw within authorized scope.

responsible_disclosure.github_bug_bounty: Use GitHub Bug Bounty/HackerOne for GitHub-owned in-scope vulnerabilities.
responsible_disclosure.pre_contact_rule: If proposed testing may exceed or be unaddressed by the published rules, contact GitHub Bug Bounty before performing it.
evidence_package: clear distinction between scheduler-side and GitHub-side behavior
